newsitem.title: FRANCE: EU scraps daily wheat refund, posts "nil value".
newsitem.headline: EU scraps daily wheat refund, posts "nil value".

text.p: The European Union's executive Commission, in a technical response to suddenly volatile wheat markets, on Monday scrapped its standing export refund for common wheat and durum wheat and replaced it with an entry known as a "dash" that has nil value, an EU official said.
The standing or daily refund for both grains previously stood at zero. But this became attractive after U.S. markets soared on fears of winterkill in the hard red winter wheat belt.
Under EU rules even a zero subsidy can be prefixed for several months ahead and comes with monthly incremental bonuses.
The new entry has no prefixable value and no increments.
The move makes it riskier for traders to use the EU's daily export channel for wheat exports, an alternative route to the weekly export subsidy tender held each Thursday in Brussels.
It comes after 160,000 tonnes of common or soft wheat were lined up for export via the daily mechanism through bids for zero refunds submitted earlier on Monday.
The EU official said these bids were expected to be passed, despite the Commission's three-day right of veto.
Anyone taking up wheat licences through the daily channel now, however, will face the risk that the value of the licence can be altered before it is used at the time of shipment.
The EU took similar steps to prevent wheat reaching world markets through the daily channel last year, as a precursor to export taxes imposed to drive down domestic prices.
But the official said it was far too early to say what consequences, if any, the latest move would have on export subsidies handed out at the weekly tender.
"We did this because of limit-up in Chicago," he said.
No further action had been decided and markets should not read too much into the decision just yet, he said.

The EU is nearing the end of its 1996/97 (July/June) export campaign, having released just under nine million tonnes of commercial soft wheat grain for export up to April 8. The figure was 60 percent more than at the same point last year.

When last Thursday's tender awards and the 160,000 tonnes taken up on Monday are included, the EU has released 9.3 million tonnes out of a total 1996/97 export goal estimated by the grain industry at around 10 million tonnes.

At Monday's firm prices, U.S. soft red winter for May -- still effectively an important pricing guide for Brussels even though the actual old crop is scarce -- was notionally worth $164-165 per tonne fob Gulf, European traders said.
French wheat for May was seen at the same level or slightly less, based on the last maximum weekly EU refund of 6.49 Ecus.
The EU this season has generally held its implied French export price several dollars above soft red winter and last week the gap between them was $9 a tonne.
